newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Aussie sees over A$500 mln business loans.
newsitem.headline: Aussie sees over A$500 mln business loans.

text.p: Aussie Home Loans Ltd (AHL) said on Monday it expected to write more than A$500 million in business loans over the next 12 months and would attack this market with the same vigour that had won it recognition in the housing sector.
"There is no competition in the business loan market and the banks are getting away with murder," managing director John Symond told Reuters.
AHL would offer a variable loan of 7.49 percent which was mostly aimed at the small business sector and which would be secured by the borrower's first mortgage.

AHL, which was now ranked as the fifth largest mortgage lender with the success of its "no-frills" loans, said its business loans would be funded by its existing exclusive securitisation programme with the PUMA Management unit of Macquarie Bank Ltd.
"I am expecting 15 to 20 percent of our new loans written to be business loans, so that would put it at about A$50 million plus a month," Symond told Reuters.
"I would expect the first 12 months to be somewhere between A$500 million and A$1 billion," he said.
Symond said Australian banks would have to respond quickly to AHL's emergence in the business market and that their balance sheet would show the effect of this response.
"I would predict that the bank's margins would contract by at least two percent. They are (now) getting on average between four and seven percent," he said.
"We will come up to speed in volume in business lending far faster than it took us to get off the ground when we were an unknown in the home loan market," he said.
National Australia Bank Ltd, Australia's largest and most profitable bank, said it always welcomed new competitors and added that it had a business investment loan as low as 7.75 percent.
"We are not in the discouint business. We market ourselves as a full relationship bank rather than a no-frills or discount bank," NAB spokesman Haydn Park said.
